summary: Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University, Harvard University, and under Wm. Theodore de Bary. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (1955).

Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who studied at Knox College and earned his doctorate at Washington University in St. Louis. He chaired at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting appointments at Pembroke College, Oxford, and Sapienza University of Rome.

Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Patrick Olivelle, Ludo Rocher, and Richard W. Lariviere, and has held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Texas at Austin.

Donald S. Lopez Jr. works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later serving as professor at Middlebury College and as a distinguished professor at the University of Michigan.

Donald Wiebe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He held a post at Trinity College, Toronto, from approximately 1980 to 2013 and served as general editor for Toronto Studies in Religion.
Dondub Buddhayin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who served as abbot of Ganden Dargye Ling and Chilttai Monastery.

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Dongak Tendzin studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and also taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Dongchu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean at Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy and abbot at Dinghui Monastery.

Donna C. Kurtz is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Cincinnati, Yale University, and Somerville College. She held a post at the Classical Art Research Centre from around 1970 to 2011.

Dor Bahadur Bista is a Tibetology scholar who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He was a professor at Tribhuvan University from approximately 1975 to 1993 and served on the board of governors of ICIMOD.
Doranne Jacobson is an Indology scholar who earned a doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Hunter College and the University of Pennsylvania, she held posts at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Stony Brook University, Columbia, Barnard, George Washington, and George Mason.
Doris Unterthurner works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her master's degree at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Ja Shong Lob Zur Lodrö Gyatso, Nying Ri Tri Chen Tutob Tendzin, Chime Tenpai Nyima, and Sakya Dak Chen Ngawang Kün Ga Gyaltsen.
Dorje Tseten was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology who studied at Beijing Normal University. He served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École militaire russo-mongole, First Kazan Male Gymnasium, and Kazan Imperial University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski.

Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and David P. Jackson, later becoming a professor at the University of Hamburg.

Dorothy C. Wong is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She has held posts at the University of Hong Kong as a visiting professor of Buddhist art and at the University of Virginia as affiliate faculty.
